question: How do I replace a GFCI outlet in my bathroom that keeps tripping the circuit?
answer: To replace a GFCI outlet that keeps tripping, turn off the power to the circuit at the main electrical panel. Remove the outlet cover and any screws holding the outlet in place. Pull the outlet out of the wall and disconnect the wires. Remove the old GFCI outlet and replace it with a new one. Make sure to connect the wires to the correct terminals and set the GFCI to test mode. Test the outlet by pressing the "Test" button and then the "Reset" button. Once the outlet passes the test, set it to normal mode and replace the outlet cover.
